messages.author: 3b39745f73eec779
messages.subject: Re: Error in sumstats()
parts:
Hi Nora,


sumsats, depending on your input, may actually be plowing trough 9 million+ lines of summary statistics, this can be fairly slow depending on your machine. The usual solution is to split the files into pieces (per chromosome for example) and to run the chromosomes in parallel on a cluster. 

To make sure there is no other issue here, you could make files that contain like 10 SNPs (or even just 2) and see if those run. If they do run you need to either wait longer or run per chromosome, if they don't come back here and we'll figure out whats wrong.

Best,
Michel




On Tuesday, August 13, 2019 at 11:59:35 AM UTC+2, Nora S. wrote:

Hi Michel,

for some reason the sumstats step doesn't run through. I don't get an error message, just nothing happens (for 2 hours).


require(GenomicSEM)

files=c("ocd_aug2017","PGC_UKB_depression_genome-wide_modified.txt","adhd_eur_jun2017","iPSYCH-PGC_ASD_Nov2017")

ref= "reference.1000G.maf.0.005.txt"

trait.names <- c("OCD","MDD","ADHD","ASD")

se.logit=c(T,T,T,T)

maf.filter=.01

info-filter=.6

N=c(9725,500199,53293,46351)

prop=c(.28,.34,.36,.4)

p_sumstats <-- sumstats(files=files,ref=ref,trait.names=trait.names,se.logit=se.logit,prop=prop,N=N,info.filter=info.filter,maf.filter=maf.filter)



Any idea what I am missing? 

Best, Nora

messages.subject: Re: Error in sumstats()
